name: Pelle Lindbergh
milestone_by_age_26: Won the Vezina Trophy as the NHL's best goaltender in the 1984-85 season at age 25, becoming the first European-born goaltender to win the award and leading the Philadelphia Flyers to the Stanley Cup Final.
early_history_summary: Started playing hockey at age 4 with Hammarby IF in Stockholm, where his father had signed him up as an infant member. He rose through Sweden's junior ranks, winning European Junior Championship gold in 1977 and World Junior Championship silver in 1978, before being drafted by the Philadelphia Flyers in 1979 and making his NHL debut in 1982.
family_context_summary: Born to a working-class family in Stockholm; his father Sigge signed him up as a member of Hammarby IF athletic association as an infant and introduced him to hockey at age 4.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father was actively involved in his early hockey development, enrolling him in Hammarby IF and supporting his goaltending ambitions from childhood.
primary_early_advantage_tags: youth club development, national team pipeline, early specialization, parental support
evidence_summary: Lindbergh was immersed in hockey from infancy, with his father signing him up for Hammarby IF and starting him at age 4. He progressed rapidly through Swedish junior hockey, winning European Junior gold at 17 and World Junior silver at 18. Drafted by the Philadelphia Flyers in 1979, he developed through the AHL before becoming the NHL's top goaltender and first European Vezina Trophy winner at age 25. His father's early involvement and the Swedish hockey development pipeline were key advantages.
starting_point: Born to a working-class family in Stockholm; father Sigge was actively involved in local hockey, signing Pelle up as a Hammarby IF member as an infant.
current_position: Died in a car accident on November 11, 1985, at age 26; final role was starting goaltender for the Philadelphia Flyers and Vezina Trophy winner.

name: Oldřich Machač
milestone_by_age_26: Won Olympic silver medal at the 1968 Winter Olympics with Czechoslovakia at age 21, followed by World Championship gold and All-Star selection in 1972 at age 25-26.
early_history_summary: Began playing hockey at age 11 with TJ Železárny Prostějov in 1957. He moved to Dukla Košice in 1965 and then to TJ ZKL Brno (Kometa Brno), becoming a stalwart defenseman for the Czechoslovak national team with 293 career caps.
primary_early_advantage_tags: national team system, defensive partnership, club development
evidence_summary: Machač began his hockey career at 11 with a local club in Prostějov before moving through the Czechoslovak club system to Kometa Brno. He became a key defenseman for the Czechoslovak national team, winning Olympic silver at 21 and World Championship gold at 25-26. His long-term defensive partnership with František Pospíšil was notable. Family background is not documented in reviewed sources.
starting_point: Born in Prostějov, Czechoslovakia in 1946; family background not documented in reviewed sources.
current_position: Died on August 10, 2011, at age 65 in Brno; final status was retired hockey player inducted into the IIHF Hall of Fame in 1999.

name: Philippe Herreweghe
milestone_by_age_26: Founded the Collegium Vocale Gent in 1970 at age 22-23, which was soon invited by Nikolaus Harnoncourt and Gustav Leonhardt to participate in their landmark complete Bach cantata recordings.
early_history_summary: Born in Ghent to a doctor father and amateur pianist mother who gave him his first piano lessons. He combined medical studies at the University of Ghent with musical training at the Ghent Conservatory, where he studied piano with Marcel Gazelle, Yehudi Menuhin's accompanist. In 1970, while still a student, he founded the Collegium Vocale Gent.
family_context_summary: Born in Ghent as the first of three children; father was a doctor and mother was a music-loving amateur pianist who gave him his first piano lessons.
parent_family_domain_summary: Mother was an amateur pianist who provided early musical training; father was a doctor, providing a middle-class intellectual household.
primary_early_advantage_tags: family musical background, conservatory training, early music movement, Harnoncourt/Leonhardt network
evidence_summary: Herreweghe grew up in a cultured Ghent household with a doctor father and pianist mother who gave him early piano lessons. He combined medical and musical studies at university, founding the Collegium Vocale Gent at 22-23. His talent was recognized by Harnoncourt and Leonhardt, who invited him to join their landmark Bach cantata recordings, launching his career as a leading figure in the early music movement.
starting_point: Born in Ghent, Belgium to a doctor father and amateur pianist mother who provided his first piano lessons; grew up in a cultured middle-class household.
current_position: Active conductor leading Collegium Vocale Gent and the Orchestre des Champs Élysées; principal conductor of the Antwerp Symphony Orchestra; over 120 recordings on his own phi label and other labels.

name: Vinko Jelovac
milestone_by_age_26: Won the FIBA World Championship gold medal with Yugoslavia in 1970 at age 21, and was named to the FIBA European Selection in 1973 and 1974.
early_history_summary: Began his club career with Gradine Pula in 1967 before moving to Olimpija Ljubljana in 1969, where he won the Yugoslav First Federal League championship in his first season. He was a member of Yugoslavia's junior national teams, winning silver at the 1968 European Junior Championship.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Yugoslav national team, physical size, club system, World Championship
evidence_summary: Jelovac leveraged his exceptional 2.08m height to become a dominant center in Yugoslav basketball, starting his club career at 18 and joining Olimpija Ljubljana at 20. He won the World Championship gold with Yugoslavia at 21 and was named to the FIBA European Selection twice by age 25. The Yugoslav national team system was one of the world's best development pipelines. Family background is not documented.
starting_point: Born in Pazin, Croatia (then Yugoslavia) in 1948; family background not documented in reviewed sources.
current_position: Retired from professional basketball in 1982; later worked as a basketball coach; inducted into the Slovenian Athletes Hall of Fame in 2012.

name: Alberto Nisman

family_context_summary: Born to a middle-class Jewish family in Buenos Aires.

name: Toshihide Maskawa
milestone_by_age_26: Earned PhD in particle physics from Nagoya University in 1967 at age 27 and published the Kobayashi-Maskawa paper in 1973 at age 33; was a graduate student and postdoc before age 26 with no material milestone by that age.
early_history_summary: Born in Nagoya as the second child of a family of sugar merchants, Maskawa entered Nagoya University in 1958 and joined the particle-theory group of Shoichi Sakata. He was a graduate student and then postdoc at Nagoya University through the 1960s.
family_context_summary: Born in Nagoya as the second child; parents were traders who sold mainly sugar. He was motivated to pursue academics to avoid succeeding his father as a sugar merchant.
parent_family_domain_summary: Parents were sugar merchants; no academic or scientific background in the family.
evidence_summary: Maskawa was a graduate student at Nagoya University through his mid-twenties, earning his PhD at 27. His Nobel Prize-winning work with Kobayashi was published in 1973 when he was 33. No material milestone occurred by age 26.

name: Jean-Claude Carrière
milestone_by_age_26: Published his first novel at age 24 (~1955), which achieved notable success and led to his entry into filmmaking through Jacques Tati, launching a career that would include an Oscar by age 32.
early_history_summary: Born to a family of vintners in southwestern France, Carrière was a gifted student who attended Lycée Lakanal and then the École normale supérieure de Saint-Cloud. He published his first novel at 24, which had enough success that his publisher suggested he novelize Jacques Tati's M. Hulot films, launching his screenwriting career.
family_context_summary: Born to a family of vintners in Colombières-sur-Orb in southwestern France; parents moved to Montreuil near Paris in 1945 to start a coffeehouse.
parent_family_domain_summary: Family were vintners with no apparent connection to film or literature; parents ran a coffeehouse in the Paris suburbs.
primary_early_advantage_tags: elite education, literary talent, Tati mentorship, Paris film ecosystem
evidence_summary: Carrière was a gifted student from a vintner family who attended the elite École normale supérieure de Saint-Cloud. He published his first novel at 24, which achieved success and led to a connection with Jacques Tati, who mentored him into filmmaking. His elite education and early entry into the French film world through Tati were key advantages.
starting_point: Born to a family of vintners in Colombières-sur-Orb, southwestern France; parents moved to Paris suburbs in 1945 to open a coffeehouse.
current_position: Died on February 8, 2021, at age 89 in Paris; final career status was one of France's most prolific screenwriters with over 150 screen credits and an Honorary Oscar.

name: Park Joo-bong
milestone_by_age_26: Won World Championship silver in men's doubles in 1983 at age 18, and All England Open titles in 1985 and 1986, establishing himself as one of the world's top badminton players before age 26.
early_history_summary: Began playing badminton at age 11, encouraged by his father Park Myung-soo. He was selected for the South Korean national team in 1981 at age 16, and quickly rose to international prominence with World Championship silver in 1983 and multiple All England titles by his early 20s.
family_context_summary: Born in Imsil, North Jeolla Province, South Korea; father Park Myung-soo encouraged him to start playing badminton at age 11.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father actively encouraged his badminton career, introducing him to the sport at age 11.

evidence_summary: Park began badminton at 11, encouraged by his father, and was selected for the South Korean national team at just 16. He won World Championship silver at 18 and All England titles by his early 20s, benefiting from the Korean national team system and strong doubles partnerships. His exceptional reflexes and versatility made him one of badminton's all-time greats.

name: Harika Dronavalli
milestone_by_age_26: Became the youngest Woman International Master in Asia in 2003 at age 12 and the youngest Woman Grandmaster in Asia in 2004 at age 13, later winning the Arjuna Award at 16 and achieving the Grandmaster title at 20.
early_history_summary: Born in Guntur, Andhra Pradesh to Ramesh and Swarna Dronavalli, she started playing chess at a very young age, winning a medal in the under-9 national championship and silver at the World Youth Championship for under-10 girls. She trained under coach NVS Ramaraju and rapidly earned WIM (2003) and WGM (2004) titles as the youngest in Asia.
family_context_summary: Born in a Telugu family in Guntur, Andhra Pradesh; father Ramesh works as a deputy executive engineer at a Panchayat Raj subdivision, and he served as her first chess coach.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father introduced her to chess and was her first coach; father is a deputy executive engineer, providing a middle-class background.
primary_early_advantage_tags: early chess start, father as first coach, dedicated coaching, chess prodigy, Indian chess ecosystem
evidence_summary: Harika started chess at a very young age with her father as first coach, winning national and world youth medals by age 9-10. Under coach NVS Ramaraju, she became the youngest WIM in Asia at 12 and youngest WGM at 13. Her father's middle-class engineering job provided stability, and the rising Indian chess ecosystem offered competitive opportunities. She went on to become India's second female Grandmaster and win three World Championship bronzes.

name: Carlos Moyá
milestone_by_age_26: Won the 1998 French Open at age 21 and reached the ATP world No. 1 singles ranking in March 1999 at age 22, establishing himself as one of the dominant players of his era.
early_history_summary: Born in Palma, Mallorca, Moyá started playing tennis at age 6, winning his first tournament at 8. He left home at 14 to attend a high-performance tennis center, joined the CAR (Centro de Alto Rendimiento) in Barcelona at 17, and won the European Junior Championship. He turned pro in 1995, winning his first ATP title at 19.
family_context_summary: Born in Palma, Mallorca to parents Andrés and Pilar; grew up near the Club Gran Playa tennis courts where his father played; has an older sister Begoña and older brother Andrés.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father played tennis at the local club visible from their home; Moyá observed tennis from age 2 and started playing at 6.

evidence_summary: Moyá grew up next to tennis courts in Mallorca, starting at age 6 with his father's involvement. He left home at 14 for a high-performance center in Barcelona, joining the CAR at 17 and winning the European Junior Championship. He turned pro at 19, won his first ATP title that year, reached the Australian Open final at 20, and won the French Open at 21. The Spanish tennis development system and early immersion in the sport were key advantages.

current_position: Retired from professional tennis in 2010; served as Rafael Nadal's primary coach from 2016 to 2024; resides in Madrid.

name: Ennio Antonelli
milestone_by_age_26: Ordained as a priest in 1960 at age 23 and worked as a seminary vice-rector and teacher; first bishop appointment came in 1982 at age 45; no material milestone by age 26 found.
early_history_summary: Born in Todi, Umbria, Antonelli attended the seminary in Todi, the regional seminary in Assisi, and the pontifical major seminary in Rome. He earned a licentiate in sacred theology from the Pontifical Lateran University and a doctorate in classics from the University of Perugia before being ordained a priest in 1960.
evidence_summary: Antonelli was ordained a priest at 23 and worked in seminary education through his twenties. His first significant appointment as bishop came at 45 in 1982. No material milestone occurred by age 26.
